candidates.name: OvertureMaps/data
candidates.what_it_holds: Pointer/access-scripts repo for the Overture Maps Foundation's global 'places' theme release: GeoParquet, partitioned by theme=places on S3 (s3://overturemaps-us-west-2/release/.../theme=places/) and Azure Blob. Places theme is a global POI dataset (built from Meta, Microsoft, TomTom, OSM and other contributors) with a categories taxonomy that includes lodging/hotel-type places, name, address, geometry, confidence score, and per-release versioning (monthly releases since 2023) — so pulling successive releases gives a point-in-time hotel-POI-count series by city/country.
candidates.why_useful: Global, monthly-versioned hotel/lodging POI counts by geography could proxy hotel supply growth (gap #8) and give a competitor-supply denominator alongside Inside Airbnb STR counts; monthly releases are effectively point-in-time vintages (gap #4).
candidates.size_hint: places theme is 10s of millions of global POIs (multi-GB Parquet)
candidates.license: ODbL / CDLA depending on theme (check per-theme licence in Overture docs)
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained, monthly releases as of Sep 2026

candidates.name: OvertureMaps/overturemaps-py
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python CLI/library (pip/conda/homebrew, 266 stars) to download Overture Maps data for a bounding box or region and convert to GeoParquet/GeoJSON/etc; has `download`, `gers` (stable feature IDs across releases, useful for change-tracking), `releases`, and `changelog` subcommands.
candidates.why_useful: This is the practical one-command tool to actually pull the places theme (hotels/lodging category) for named cities/regions and diff across releases — turns the Overture places theme (row above) into something the team can script without hand-rolling Parquet/S3 access.

candidates.name: yharby/OvertureMapsDownloader
candidates.what_it_holds: 103-star tool using DuckDB, Dask and GDAL/OGR to extract/filter Overture Maps Parquet data (including the places theme) into more usable formats, an alternative/complementary path to overturemaps-py for bulk or DuckDB-native pulls.
candidates.why_useful: Same hotel-POI supply-tracking use case as OvertureMaps/data but with a DuckDB-native workflow, which matches the team's existing DuckDB tooling for Inside Airbnb.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: alternative access path to OvertureMaps/data above

candidates.name: kraina-ai/overturemaestro
candidates.what_it_holds: 36-star Python tool for reading Overture Maps data with multiprocessing, region clipping and QoL wrappers on top of the raw Parquet release, built by the same group behind `srai`/`quackosm` geospatial-ML tooling.
candidates.why_useful: Another acquisition path for the same global hotel/lodging POI data described above; useful if overturemaps-py proves too slow for country-scale pulls.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: alternative access path to OvertureMaps/data above

candidates.name: henryspatialanalysis/OpenPOIs
candidates.what_it_holds: 31-star toolkit for comparing and conflating points-of-interest across major open geospatial POI datasets (explicitly including Overture Maps, and typically OSM/Foursquare-style sources) to reduce double-counting and improve category harmonisation.
candidates.why_useful: If the team pulls hotel POIs from more than one source (Overture + OSM + Foursquare), this tool addresses the exact problem of matching/deduplicating the same physical hotel across datasets before counting supply.

candidates.name: Foursquare Open Source Places (fsq-os-places)
candidates.what_it_holds: Foursquare's open global POI dataset: 100M+ POIs, 200+ countries/territories, 1000+ place categories (Foursquare's taxonomy includes a 'Hotel'/'Lodging' branch), 20+ core attributes (name, address, lat/lon, category, chain flags). Hosted on Foursquare's own site / HuggingFace / cloud storage (Parquet), refreshed periodically (monthly-ish cadence per Foursquare's public statements); no dedicated GitHub data repo found (searched fsq-os-places / foursquare-os-places, both 404), so treat GitHub only as a discovery pointer to the external host.
candidates.why_useful: A second independent global hotel/lodging POI census (cross-check against Overture places) with a documented 'Hotel' category, letting the team build/validate a hotel-count-by-city supply series and check counts against known chain unit disclosures.
candidates.time_coverage: periodic full-dataset refreshes, no long history of vintages published
candidates.size_hint: 100M+ POIs total (lodging category a small subset)
candidates.license: Foursquare open data licence (check terms; free for commercial+non-commercial per their announcement)

candidates.name: David984-code/hospitality-alt-data-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit research dashboard for US lodging-demand alt-data on hotel franchisor equities (MAR, HLT, H): pulls TSA checkpoint throughput (2019-present), Google Trends brand search (pytrends) for Marriott/Hilton/Hyatt/Wyndham/Choice/IHG, BLS JOLTS+CES leisure & hospitality employment, BLS PPI Traveler Accommodation (ADR/room-rate proxy), yfinance prices/earnings dates for a 3-name + 20-name REIT/franchisor universe, and a COMMITTED file `data/reported_revpar.csv` of hand-keyed quarterly reported RevPAR from MAR/HLT/H earnings releases, Q1 2019-Q2 2026. 32 commits, active Sep 2026, 1 open PR.
candidates.why_useful: Directly matches gap #8 (regional RevPAR, hotel demand) with an actual committed multi-year reported-RevPAR CSV plus a live, no-key pipeline (TSA/BLS/Trends/yfinance) for hotel-brand demand proxies that read through to STR competitive pricing pressure.
candidates.size_hint: small (single CSV of quarterly RevPAR by brand + regenerable pipeline outputs)
candidates.license: not stated in README (research tool, not investment advice)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: TSA and Google Trends pieces overlap what we already hold; the hand-keyed reported RevPAR csv for MAR/HLT/H is the new piece (we hold MAR/HLT RevPAR 'from releases' per CONTEXT but not necessarily this exact vintage/format)

candidates.name: whosonfirst-data (org, e.g. whosonfirst-data-venue-us-ca)
candidates.what_it_holds: Mapzen-originated open gazetteer, 823+ per-country/state git repos of GeoJSON 'venue' records (a placetype that includes hotels), sourced partly via a historical Foursquare data partnership. Example: whosonfirst-data-venue-us-ca (691 commits) holds California venue GeoJSON records. Because every record edit is a git commit, the commit history itself is a de facto point-in-time log of when a venue (hotel) appeared/closed/moved — unusual for POI data.
candidates.why_useful: A git-versioned historical venue gazetteer that plausibly includes US/global hotels going back to ~2015-2017 is a genuine point-in-time hotel-POI source (gap #4 + #8 combined), unlike Overture/Foursquare which only publish current snapshots.
candidates.geography: global, split by country then US by state
candidates.time_coverage: ~2015-2017 onward per commit history; project itself looks dormant (mapzen.com is defunct) with the newest visible activity as late as Aug 2026 in some repos, so still receiving occasional automated updates
candidates.size_hint: 823+ repos; per-state venue repo sizes not confirmed, likely thousands of records each
candidates.license: check LICENSE.md per repo (historically CC0-ish for WOF admin data; venue data licence terms vary by contributor)
candidates.last_activity: mixed; some repos updated as recently as Aug 2026, overall project largely dormant since Mapzen's 2017 shutdown

candidates.name: hrecht/censusapi
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (186 stars, CRAN + GitHub) giving lightweight access to 1,500+ US Census Bureau API endpoints via `getCensus()`/`listCensusApis()`/`listCensusMetadata()`. Endpoint list is generic (ACS, SAIPE, SAHIE, international trade, economic time series) but because it hits Census's full API catalog by URL/dataset code, it can reach County Business Patterns (CBP) and Quarterly Services Survey/Services Annual Survey endpoints (NAICS 721 accommodation establishment counts, employment, receipts) even though the README doesn't name CBP/QSS explicitly.
candidates.why_useful: A ready client for pulling NAICS 721 (accommodation) establishment counts/employment/payroll by county from Census CBP/QSS/SAS — exactly the 'lodging census' tooling the theme asks for — without hand-rolling Census API calls.
candidates.time_coverage: whatever vintages Census publishes for CBP (annual, ~2-year lag) / QSS (quarterly)

candidates.name: datamade/census
candidates.what_it_holds: Python wrapper (682 stars) for the US Census Bureau API — ACS 1/3/5-year, ACS profiles/subject tables, 2010 SF1, and 2000/2010/2020 redistricting (PL) data. README as fetched does not mention CBP or QSS/NAICS support specifically, so its usefulness for NAICS 721 lodging counts is unconfirmed and may require the generic/undocumented Census API passthrough.
candidates.why_useful: Popular, well-maintained generic Census API client; worth checking directly (not via this fetch) whether its generic query path reaches CBP/QSS series for NAICS 721 lodging establishment counts by county, as a lower-effort alternative to hrecht/censusapi.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps hrecht/censusapi above as a generic Census API client

candidates.name: sakera023/us-small-business-capital-access-atlas
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit/Python geospatial platform analyzing small-business capital access, financing gaps and entrepreneurial opportunity across US states/communities, built on Census and SBA public data; the only repo found tagged 'county-business-patterns' on GitHub, implying it ingests CBP data by NAICS sector (accommodation/721 would be one of many sectors covered, not a dedicated focus).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: if it has a working CBP ingestion pipeline, that pipeline (not the small-business-finance framing) could be repurposed to pull NAICS 721 accommodation establishment/employment counts by county; not verified beyond the topic tag and description.

notes: Hard environment constraint this run: the session's shared WebSearch tool budget (200/200) was already exhausted by other parallel scouts before any of my queries ran, so every WebSearch call failed immediately with a budget-exhausted error — none of the four intended opening queries executed. I fell back to WebFetch against github.com/topics/*, github.com/search (which itself 429'd repeatedly, Retry-After 3600, after ~2 calls — treat github.com/search as unusable via WebFetch for the rest of this run), Bing search result pages, and DuckDuckGo (both html.duckduckgo.com and lite.duckduckgo.com returned CAPTCHA challenge pages instead of results, so DDG is a dead end for automated fetch). Bing search-result pages fetched via WebFetch frequently rendered only generic/irrelevant boilerplate (ads, homepage links, unrelated cached content) rather than the actual ranked results, so several Bing queries produced no usable signal despite claiming '~100k-500k results' — this looks like Bing serving a non-JS/degraded results page to the fetcher rather than true zero-relevance. Net effect: coverage of this theme is narrower than a full WebSearch pass would give. Two productive channels were GitHub's static /topics/<tag> pages (no rate limit hit) and direct WebFetch of specific known-likely repo URLs (Overture Maps org, Foursquare docs, Who's On First, Census API wrappers) guessed from domain knowledge. Not found despite trying: a dedicated hotel-construction-pipeline dataset (STR/CoStar-style openly published pipeline data appears to not exist on GitHub, unsurprising since that data is commercially licensed), any GitHub repo specifically publishing Census QSS (Quarterly Services Survey) NAICS 721 data (the 'qss' topic tag means Qt Style Sheets on GitHub, a false-friend worth remembering for future scouts), and no confirmed OSM-Overpass-specific hotel-extraction repo (OSM tourism=hotel tag access is generic Overpass API usage, not something that produced a dedicated repo in topic searches). Suggest a future run with WebSearch budget available re-run the four original hinted queries plus 'STR CoStar hotel pipeline open data', 'AHLA hotel supply data open', and 'Lodging Econometrics API' directly.
